requirementText:
# REQ-101: Partial refunds for captured payments

**Requested by:** Merchant Experience PM
**Priority:** P1 (top merchant ask this quarter)

Merchants today can only refund the full amount of a payment. They need to refund part
of a captured payment, for example when one item of a multi-item order is returned.

- A captured payment can be refunded in one or more parts.
- The total refunded must never exceed the captured amount.
- Merchants' systems retry on network failures, so a retried refund request must not
  refund twice.
- Finance needs every refund to appear in the ledger.
- Card numbers must never appear in logs (PCI DSS).
statusReason: All gates passed. Merge and deployment need human approval.

iterations.developerSummary: Add refund service with cumulative-balance guard and idempotency keys; also clarify the settlement module comment
policyViolations: src/settlement.js is not in the architect's allowed_files; unrelated file changes are blocked
feedback: src/settlement.js is not in the architect's allowed_files; unrelated file changes are blocked

iterations.developerSummary: Add refund service with cumulative-balance guard, per-payment idempotency keys and REFUND ledger entries

qa.feedback_for_developer: All 15 tests pass, coverage 93.36%, no lint issues.

security.summary: No blocking findings. Diff reviewed for PAN exposure, secrets, injection and authorisation.

analysis.summary: Allow merchants to refund a captured payment in one or more parts, never exceeding the captured amount, safely under client retries, with every refund in the ledger and no card data in logs.

acceptance_criteria.then: the refund succeeds, refundedAmount is 3000 paise and the status is PARTIALLY_REFUNDED

acceptance_criteria.given: a payment with INR 60.00 of 100.00 already refunded
acceptance_criteria.when: the merchant requests a further INR 50.00 refund
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is rejected and refundedAmount stays 6000 paise

acceptance_criteria.given: a refund request with idempotency key K
acceptance_criteria.when: the same request with key K is retried
acceptance_criteria.then: the original refund is returned and no second refund or ledger entry is created

acceptance_criteria.given: a payment that is not captured, or an amount that is zero or not whole paise

acceptance_criteria.then: a REFUND ledger entry with the refunded amount exists and no log line contains the card number

tasks.title: Identify impacted modules and define the refund API
Implement partial refunds with idempotency keys
Run unit, acceptance, coverage and lint checks
Security review of the diff (PCI: PAN exposure)
Assemble release evidence and request approval

assumptions: Amounts are integer paise, as in the existing service.
Idempotency keys are unique per payment, not globally.
Existing full-refund behaviour (refundPayment) must keep working.
open_questions: Should partial refunds be limited by the 180-day refund window in config/gateway.config.json? Assumed out of scope for this change.
out_of_scope: Asynchronous refund settlement with the acquirer

impacted_components.reason: New refund service: partial refunds, cumulative guard, idempotency index.
Add PARTIALLY_REFUNDED status and refundedAmount field; keep refundPayment behaviour.
Developer unit tests for the refund service.
Refunds are recorded with the existing REFUND entry type.
Already nets REFUND entries per merchant; no change needed.
Use redact() or log identifiers only.

design.approach: Add a createRefundService(store) module that validates the amount, checks the payment is CAPTURED or PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, enforces refundedAmount + amount <= amount, deduplicates on (paymentId, idempotencyKey), updates the payment status and writes a REFUND ledger entry referencing the refund id.
api_contract: createRefundService(store) -> { refund({ paymentId, amount, idempotencyKey }) -> { id, paymentId, amount, idempotencyKey, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }, listRefunds(paymentId) -> refund[] }
refund() throws when idempotencyKey is missing, the amount is invalid, the payment is not refundable, or the amount exceeds the remaining balance
payments gain refundedAmount (paise) and the PaymentStatus.PARTIALLY_REFUNDED status

forbidden_files.reason: Owned by the Finance platform team; entry types are a closed set (ADR-2).
Owned by the Settlements team; unaffected by this change.

decisions.decision: Partial refunds live in a new module, src/refunds.js
decisions.rationale: Keeps payments.js small and isolates the new behaviour for review and rollback.

decisions.decision: Use the existing REFUND ledger entry type for partial refunds
decisions.rationale: Ledger entry types are agreed with Finance; settlement already nets REFUND entries correctly.

decisions.decision: Idempotency keys are scoped per payment and stored in memory for now
decisions.rationale: Matches the in-memory store; flagged as a known risk for multi-instance deployment.

risks: In-memory idempotency index is lost on restart.
Concurrent refunds on one payment are not serialised.

criteria.name: Acceptance criteria verified by passing tests

release.title: REQ-101: partial refunds (4 files)
release.summary: Adds partial refunds with cumulative-amount guard and idempotency keys. Converged in 2 iteration(s).
test_evidence: 15/15 tests passed (regression, developer unit and QA acceptance suites)
Static security scan: 0 finding(s); lint: 0 issue(s)
known_risks: Idempotency index is in memory; it must move to the database before multi-instance deployment.
Concurrent refunds on the same payment are not serialised (single-threaded sample service).
release.rollback_plan: Revert the merge commit; no schema or ledger entry-type changes were made, so no data migration is needed.
